title: De motu vibratorio laminarum elasticarum, ubi plures novae vibrationum species hactenus non pertractatae evolvuntur

deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening page of E443 (Novi Commentarii 17, 1772/73, pp. 449ff.). Euler explains that he treated elastic laminae long ago (the 1744 'Additamentum I, De curvis elasticis' to the Methodus inveniendi, where he discussed vibrations of elastic bands). He now returns to the problem because 'the true method of solving such questions has only recently begun to be cultivated', meaning the partial-differential-equation approach to continuous vibrating bodies.

§1 sets up the model:
- A uniform lamina, with the same thickness and the same elastic strength along its whole length.
- The mass is given as a linear density: a length k of lamina has mass (or weight) K, so a length x has mass Kx/k.
- In its natural state the lamina is straight.
- Its elasticity resists bending so that the moment needed to hold a given curvature is inversely proportional to the radius of curvature, M = (const)·cc/r.

In modern terms this is the Bernoulli–Euler constitutive law M = EI·κ. Euler's constant written K·c² (or C·c²) plays the role of the flexural rigidity EI.

On the next page this law, together with the small-deflection approximation r ≈ dx²/d²y, gives the moment Kcc·y''. This leads to the beam equation (K/k)·y_tt = −Kcc·y'''' and hence to the various end conditions and vibration modes the paper develops.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The only issue is the rigidity symbol. The transcription reads it as 'Ecc', the scan glyph looks like 'Ccc', and the next page writes 'Kcc'. It is presumably a single typographical inconsistency in the constant; nothing of substance depends on it.

ideas.what: Bending moment inversely proportional to the radius of curvature for an elastic lamina (moment = const·c²/r).
ideas.modern_name: Bernoulli–Euler moment–curvature law, M = EI κ
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jakob Bernoulli (1690s); Daniel Bernoulli and Euler (1742–44)
ideas.where_published: Euler, Methodus inveniendi (1744), Additamentum I 'De curvis elasticis'; Opera omnia II.11 with Truesdell's historical commentary

ideas.what: Uniform linear mass density introduced via a reference length k having mass K; return to the vibrating-lamina problem using the newer PDE method.
ideas.modern_name: Linear density ρA; continuum (PDE) treatment of transverse beam vibrations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Daniel Bernoulli and Euler (1735–1744 for beam vibrations); d'Alembert and Euler (1747–1750s for the PDE method)
ideas.where_published: E443 itself; Truesdell, 'The rational mechanics of flexible or elastic bodies 1638–1788' (Opera omnia II.11.2)

deep.surprise_reason: This is an introductory set-up page restating the standard elastica constitutive law and the mass normalization. All of it is well documented in Euler's 1744 work and in Truesdell's history.
transcription_corrections: 'momentum virium = Ecc/r': the scan reads more like 'Ccc/r', while the next page uses 'Kcc'. The rigidity constant is presumably intended to be Kcc (or C·cc).
Header '( o )' is a printer's ornament around the page number 449.
